newsitem.title: USA: Dean Witter eyes growth in Internet broking.
newsitem.headline: Dean Witter eyes growth in Internet broking.

text.p: Dean Witter Discover & Co's agreement to acquire Internet broker Lombard Brokerage Inc is a recognition that buying and selling stocks via personal computer has grown explosively and will continue doing so, analysts and industry executives said on Monday.

"I think it's possible that within five years 20 percent of all retail equity transactions could be executed and processed on the Internet," said Perrin Long, an independent analyst who tracks the securities industry.
He said Dean Witter's foray into Internet trading appeared to be the "right move" considering the rapid growth expected for the business.
A spokesman for Dean Witter said Lombard would be "totally separate and distinct" from Dean Witter's other main business,.
Dean Witter has 9,000 stockbrokers, ranking the firm third in the United States behind Merrill Lynch and Co Inc and Smith Barney & Co, a unit of Travelers Group Inc.
"This gives us access to new market segments, electronic delivery, electronic distribution," said Dean Witter spokesman Timothy Lee.
Dean Witter has three million customer accounts, compared with 45,000 accounts at Lombard, a Dean Witter spokesman said.

Asked if Lombard would cannibalize business from Dean Witter, the spokesman said the three million account holders are "people who value the advice and the guidance of brokers. That's why they're there."

Long agreed that the retail stock broker was not an endangered species. "That will never happen," the analyst said, adding that there will always be people who need investment advice and who will pay for it willingly.
A trade, for example, to buy 100 shares of stock with a full-service broker can cost several hundred dollars.

Under the most recent pricing schedule announced by Lombard, customers willing to trade electronically were being charged $14.95 to trade up to 5,000 shares for exchange- listed stocks and for Nasdaq issues.
Lombard has said it is adding new users to its service at the rate of 600 a day.
Other big players in electronic broking include Charles Schwab Corp, E*Trade and PC Financial Network, a unit of Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
Major full-service firms are expected to get into online trading either through purchases of existing firms or building separate units from the ground up.
Both Dean Witter and Lombard declined to disclose terms of the transaction.
A news release issued in August said San Francisco-based Lombard had revenue of $24 million in 1995. The firm said online trading over the Internet accounted for 20 percent of its revenue and trades.
